rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “He makes the foul one pile upon another,” بعضه is an appositive of الخبيث.
rows.anchor: وبعضه بدل من الخبيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على بعض means “on top of one another.”
rows.anchor: وقوله على بعض أي فوق بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here جعل means “cast” or “placed,” supported by a parallel verse describing the mountains as cast onto the earth.
rows.anchor: أي القى بدليل قوله في الآية الاخرى التي علل فيها المراد بخلق الجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is sound because the substances of night and day precede their qualities essentially: darkness and light.
rows.anchor: والجواب إن الليل جوهر قام به السواد والنهار جوهر قام به النور

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra cites Arabs’ “I did you a kindness, then clothed you” as ordering what is essentially prior, although kindness is externally the clothing itself.
rows.anchor: نقل الفراء انهم قالوا احسنت اليك فكسوتك فجعلوا الاحسان متقدما على الكسوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative objects that kindness need not be the clothing itself; it may be an inner meaning that gives rise to clothing.
rows.anchor: ولك إن تقول لانسلم أن الاحسان نفس الكسوة بل معنى يقوم بالنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حسب takes two objects when followed by أن plus a verb, as in “Did you think you would enter Paradise?” and “you would be left alone?”
rows.anchor: حسب يتعدى لمفعولين وحيث جاء بعدها إن الفعل

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh holds that the أن-clause fills the place of both objects of حسب.
rows.anchor: فمذهب سيبويه انها سادة مسد المفعولين

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad holds that the أن-clause fills one object position, with the second object understood.
rows.anchor: ومذهب المبرد انها سادة مسد المفعول الواحد والثاني عنده مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors Sibawayh: Arabs are not heard explicitly stating the second object posited by al-Mubarrad.
rows.anchor: ويشهد لسيبويه إن العرب لم يسمع من كلامهم نطق بما ادعاه من التصريح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One doctrine says كاد behaves like other verbs: affirming it affirms the near action, and negating it negates it.
rows.anchor: احدها إن اثباتها اثبات ونفيها نفي كغيرها من الافعال

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says كاد indicates that an action occurs with difficulty.
rows.anchor: والثاني انها تفيد الدلالة على وقوع الفعل بعسر وهو مذهب ابن جني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third doctrine reverses polarity: كاد يفعل means the act did not occur, while لم يكد يفعل means it did.
rows.anchor: والثالث إن اثباتها نفي ونفيها اثبات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation places God’s address to Jesus at the time He raised him to Himself.
rows.anchor: قيل قال له ذلك لما رفعه إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ can mean حين, “when.”
rows.anchor: إلا كنا عليكم شهودا إذ تفيضون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ can function as a causal particle, “because.”
rows.anchor: لن ينفعكم اليوم إذ ظلمتم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view makes إذ a temporal adverb for a future event, equivalent to إذا, including in the verse about the shackles.
rows.anchor: وقيل تأتي ظرفا لما يستقبل بمعنى اذا

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli rejects that future-time parsing, arguing that إذا does not occur with a present verb under negation; after an oath its conditional force is absent.
rows.anchor: وانكره السهيلي لان اذا لا يجئ بعدها المضارع مع النفي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some treat إذ in the creation account as extra; another analysis takes it to mean قد.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي فيه بمعنى قد

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli transmits from Sibawayh that إذ can mean إن, and applies that reading to this phrase and the warning about shared punishment.
rows.anchor: حكاه السهيلي في الروض عن نص سيبويه في كتابه

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli faults al-Farisi for making a future verb govern a past-time adverb across فـ, especially with سـ; he calls such ordering objectionable.
rows.anchor: وغفل الفارسي عما في الكتاب من هذا وجعل الفعل المستقبل الذي بعد لن

rows.speaker: الروافض
rows.claim: The author condemns the Rafidah’s allegory identifying the two seas with Ali and Fatima.
rows.anchor: مثل تأويل الروافض لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الروافض
rows.claim: The author rejects their reading of the pearls and coral as Hasan and Husayn.
rows.anchor: يعني الحسن والحسين رضي الله عنهما

words: وَإِذَا تَوَلَّىٰ سَعَىٰ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ فِيهَا
rows.speaker: الروافض
rows.claim: The author says interpreting the corrupter in this verse as Muawiya is a false, sectarian allegory.
rows.anchor: النسل ﴾ انه معاوية وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم محمد بن حبيب النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Naysaburi denounces contemporary pretended exegetes for ignorance of recitation and meaning, sensationalism for public favor, and seeking worldly gain without study.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو القاسم محمد بن حبيب النيسابوري رحمه الله وقد نبغ في زماننا مفسرون لو سئلوا عن الفرق بين التفسير والتأويل ما اهتدوا اليه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic report likens someone claiming what they were not given to wearing two garments of falsehood; no grading is supplied.
rows.anchor: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم المتشبع بما لم يعط كلابس ثوبي زور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unattributed poem warns that pretension to qualities one lacks is exposed by tests and defeated in the race.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل … من تحلى بغير ماهو فيه … فضحته شواهد الامتحان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One person absurdly explained al-Ḥāqqah as a gathering whose participants say they were at the ḥāqqah.
rows.anchor: فقال الحاقة جماعة من الناس اذا صاروا في المجلس قالوا كنا في الحاقة

rows.speaker: آخر
rows.claim: Another person reversed Noah’s command, saying the earth was told to pour water and the sky to release it.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر في قوله تعالى ﴿ يا أرض ابلعي ماءك ويا سماء أقلعي ﴾ قال امر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another false explanation says God asks people in this life about the girls buried alive among them.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم في قوله تعالى ﴿ وإذا الموؤودة سئلت ﴾ قال ان الله

words: من في السماوات ومن في الأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase repeats من in Yunus, al-Hajj, al-Naml, and al-Zumar.
rows.anchor: فى يونس والحج والنمل والزمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما occurs twice in al-Maida and also in Sad and al-Zukhruf.
rows.anchor: فى المائدة اثنان فى ص وآخر الزخرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concordance lists أرسلنا قبلك without من in Bani Israil, al-Anbiya, al-Furqan, and Saba.
rows.anchor: بإسقاط من فى بنى إسرائيل والأنبياء والفرقان وسبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أهؤلاء is written with an alif before هاء in al-Maida, al-Anam, al-Araf, and Saba.
rows.anchor: بألف قبل الهاء فى المائدة والأنعام والأعراف وسبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من تحتهم occurs in al-Anam, al-Araf, Yunus, and al-Kahf; تجري تحتها الأنهار occurs once in Bara'a.
rows.anchor: فى الأنعام والأعراف ويونس والكهف وأما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أو أن, with hamza before waw, occurs in Hud, Bani Israil, Ta Ha, and al-Mumin; examples include Hud and al-Mumin.
rows.anchor: بهمزة قبل الواو فى هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن الله كان عليما حكيما appears twice in al-Nisa and also in al-Ahzab and al-Insan.
rows.anchor: فى النساء اثنان وفى الأحزاب والإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آباؤهم occurs in the nominative in the listed examples from al-Baqara, al-Maida, Hud, and Ya Sin.
rows.anchor: بالرفع فى البقرة ﴿ أولو كان آباؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قل يا أيها الناس occurs in al-Araf, twice in Yunus, and in al-Hajj.
rows.anchor: فى الأعراف وفى يونس اثنان منها وفى الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نصرف الآيات occurs three times in al-Anam and a fourth time in al-Araf.
rows.anchor: فى الأنعام ثلاثة والرابع فى الأعراف

words: إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين occurs in al-Maida, al-Anam, al-Qasas, and al-Ahqaf.
rows.anchor: فى المائدة والأنعام والقصص والأحقاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مباركا is accusative in the listed occurrences in Ali Imran, Maryam, al-Muminun, and Qaf.
rows.anchor: بالنصب فى آل عمران ومريم والمؤمنين وق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مبارك is nominative twice in al-Anam and also in al-Anbiya and Sad.
rows.anchor: بالرفع في الأنعام اثنان وفي الأنبياء وص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما كسبت, without an initial ب, appears in al-Baqara, twice in Ali Imran, and in Ibrahim.
rows.anchor: بحذف الباء من أوله فى البقرة وآل عمران اثنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase من ذكر أو أنثى is written with an alif before waw in Ali Imran, al-Nisa, al-Nahl, and Ghafir.
rows.anchor: بإثبات الهمزة قبل الواو فى آل عمران والنساء والنحل وغافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألم يروا without an initial waw occurs in al-Anam, al-Araf, al-Naml, and Ya Sin.
rows.anchor: بغير واو فى الأنعام والأعراف والنمل ويس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولبئس occurs twice in al-Baqara and once in al-Hajj and al-Nur; فلبئس with فـ occurs only in al-Nahl.
rows.anchor: بالفاء فموضع واحد فى النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although المطلقات يتربصن is phrased as a report, it cannot literally predict that all divorced women will wait; it therefore means a command, preserving the truth of divine speech.
rows.anchor: فإن صيغته صيغة الخبر ولكن لايمكن حمله على حقيقته فإنهن قد لايتربصن

words: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ٱلْكَرِيمِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One mode of Quranic address is general address intended generally, illustrated by the call to humanity in 82:6.
rows.anchor: الأول خطاب العام المراد به العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another mode is specific address intended for its specific addressee, illustrated by the rebuke, threat, command to the Messenger, and Zayd’s divorce.
rows.anchor: الثاني خطاب الخاص والمراد به الخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third mode addresses the Prophet specifically while intending all who hold divorce authority, as in “O Prophet, when you divorce women.”
rows.anchor: الثالث خطاب الخاص والمراد به العموم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصيرفي
rows.claim: Al-Sayrafi says the address first appears specific to the Prophet, but “exclusive for you” at the end shows that the preceding permissions apply to him and others.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الصيرفي كان ابتداء الخطاب له

words: الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two people-groups differ: the first are the callers, Nuaym ibn Said al-Thaqafi, and the second Abu Sufyan and his followers.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأول نعيم بن سعيد الثقفي والثاني أبو سفيان وأصحابه

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi argues the second الناس means one person, since the following demonstrative ذلكم points to one individual; a plural referent would require plural wording.
rows.anchor: قال الفارسي ومما يقوى ان المراد بالناس في قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the plural relative form الذين is used in place of singular الذي.
rows.anchor: وقيل بل وضع فيه الذين موضع الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the rebuke “Believe as the people believed,” الناس refers to Abdullah ibn Salam.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ وإذا قيل لهم آمنوا كما آمن الناس ﴾ يعني عبد الله بن سلام

words: إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات
rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the people calling from behind the chambers as al-Aqra ibn Habis.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك وهو الأقرع بن حابس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general call to people to fear their Lord does not include children or the mentally ill.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم ﴾ لم يدخل فيه الأطفال والمجانين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A general command to give women dowries is restricted by the closing consent clause to sane adult women, since others’ consent is legally void.
rows.anchor: ثم خص في آخرها بقوله ﴿ فإن طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفسا ﴾ الآية فخصها بالعاقلة البالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting rule first addresses all divorced women, then the husbands’ right to take them back limits it to revocable divorce, since an irrevocable divorce cannot be reversed.
rows.anchor: فإنه عام في البائنة والرجعية ثم خصها بالرجعية بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on taking back what husbands gave is initially limited to the husband’s gift; the following khulʿ clause covers anything belonging to her that she gives up.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا خاص في الذي أعطاها الزوج ثم قال بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A separate verse narrows the general warning against turning one’s back in battle: the later rule sets a threshold of twenty steadfast believers.
rows.anchor: الآية فهذا عام في المقاتل كثيرا أو قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general ban on carrion is restricted by the trained hunting animal exception, which permits game killed in its mouth.
rows.anchor: وهذا عام في جميع الميتات ثم خصة بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission for sea game and its food is understood to include sea carrion, thus restricting the general prohibition.
rows.anchor: وخصص ايضا عمومه في آية اخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission to enter uninhabited houses containing an amenity is another example of specification.
rows.anchor: ومثله قوله تعالى ﴿ أن تدخلوا بيوتا غير مسكونة فيها متاع لكم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general prohibition of blood is restricted to flowing blood; liver and spleen are thereby lawful.
rows.anchor: يعني إلا الكبد والطحال فهو حلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specific exception in Meccan al-Anam precedes the general rule in Medinan al-Maida; this accords with al-Shafii’s view that a specific text qualifies a general one whether earlier or later.
rows.anchor: ثم هذه الآية خاصة في سورة الأنعام وهي مكية والآية العامة في سورة المائدة وهي مدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general statement that a wife may have been given a great amount is qualified by her freely consenting to give some of it back.
rows.anchor: وهذا عام سواء رضيت المرأة أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting rule for divorced women is general, then excludes women divorced before consummation and specifies the periods for menopausal women, minors, and pregnant women.
rows.anchor: فهذا عام في المدخول بها وغيرها ثم خصها فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting period for widows generally includes pregnant and nonpregnant women, but the rule for pregnant women ends at delivery.
rows.anchor: وهذا عام في الحامل والحائل ثم خص بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad permission to marry women is restricted by the verses prohibiting close relatives.
rows.anchor: وهذا عام في ذوات المحارم والأجنبيات ثم خص بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general penalty for fornicators includes free women and slave women; the half-penalty verse specifies the latter.
rows.anchor: عام في الحرائر والإماء ثم خصه بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic declarative forms can stand for commands, as in the instruction that mothers nurse their children.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى ﴿ والوالدات يرضعن أولادهن ﴾ 1

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declarative form المطلقات يتربصن is another example of a report used to express a command.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والمطلقات يتربصن ﴾ 2

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting سلام عليكم is listed as a declarative expression serving as a directive.
rows.anchor: ﴿ سلام عليكم ﴾ 3

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s “no reproach upon you today” is included among reports used in place of a request or command.
rows.anchor: ﴿ اليوم يغفر الله لكم ﴾ 4

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expiation stated as feeding ten needy people is a declarative construction that scholars count among examples of obligation.
rows.anchor: ولهذا جعلها العلماء من أمثلة الواجب

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: On Nafi’s reading, the clauses mean “do not engage in sexual talk or disobedience.”
rows.anchor: على قراءة نافع أي لا ترفثوا ولا تفسقوا

words: وما تنفقون إلا ابتغاء وجه الله
rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They construe the declarative wording as a prohibition: spend only seeking God’s countenance.
rows.anchor: قالوا هو خبر وتأويله نهى أي لا تنفقوا إلا ابتغاء وجه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites “none touch it except the purified” as a parallel declarative form carrying a prohibitive sense.
rows.anchor: كقوله ﴿ لا يمسه إلا المطهرون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the nominative reading of لا تضار, the phrase is understood as a prohibition against harming a mother through her child.
rows.anchor: على قراءة الرفع وقيل إنه نهى مجزوم أعنى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the covenant, لا تعبدون carries the meaning of the imperative لا تعبدوا, supported by the following command to speak well to people.
rows.anchor: ضمن لا تعبدون معنى لا تعبدوا بدليل قوله بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If حسنا is governed by أحسنوا, coordinating قولوا with it is preferable because their forms and meanings agree; if the estimate is ويحسنون, proximity favors attachment to the preceding phrase.
rows.anchor: لكن إن كان حسنا معمولا لأحسنوا فعطف قولوا عليه أولى لاتفاقهما لفظا ومعنى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the report-shaped prohibition is stronger than an explicit command because it implies the hearers will promptly stop.
rows.anchor: وقيل ﴿ لا تعبدون ﴾ أبلغ من صريح النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant phrase لا تسفكون دماءكم likewise means the imperative لا تسفكوا.
rows.anchor: وكذا قوله ﴿ وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم لا تسفكون دماءكم ﴾ 1 في موضع لا تسفكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وبشر المؤمنين is coordinated with تؤمنون بالله ورسوله, which accounts for the jussive response.
rows.anchor: وقوله في سورة الصف ﴿ وبشر المؤمنين ﴾ 2 عطفا على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection context and فـ connect “today no soul is wronged” to the universal assembly, preparing for the following address to all gathered people.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فاليوم لا تظلم نفس شيئا ﴾ 5 فإنه كلام وقت الحشر

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki treats the paradise and criminal addresses as detailing “you are repaid only for what you did,” implicitly meaning the blessed among the assembly and their separation from the others.
rows.anchor: هكذا قرره السكاكي في المفتاح

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A tafsir says the words are spoken as the people are led to Paradise, presenting a future outcome as already realized; “separate” means depart from the others toward Paradise.
rows.anchor: ثم جاء في التفسير أن قوله هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feminine plural subjects, whether small or large groups, most often take a feminine plural verb, as in these two verses.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والوالدات يرضعن ﴾ 1 ﴿ والمطلقات يتربصن ﴾ 2 هذا هو الأكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran sometimes uses a singular feminine form with a feminine plural noun, saying مطهرة rather than مطهرات.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في القران بالافراد قال تعالى ﴿ وأزواج مطهرة ﴾ 3 ولم يقل مطهرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For irrational plurals, a large group takes a singular pronoun and a small group a plural one: منها refers to twelve months, while فيهن refers to four.
rows.anchor: فالضمير في منها يعود إلى الاثني عشر وهو جمع كثرة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains the agreement by the numeral classifier: large numbers take a singular classifier such as درهم, while three to ten take plural دراهم.
rows.anchor: ذكر الفراء له سرا لطيفا فقال لما كان المميز مع جمع الكثرة واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording أبحر rather than بحور suits the small-number plural and the verse’s arrangement.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا قوله سبحانه ﴿ سبعة أبحر ﴾ 5 فاتى بجمع القلة ولم يقل بحور

rows.speaker: الحريري
rows.claim: Al-Hariri explains the plural of abundance قروء by saying each divorced woman must wait through three periods, though the rule is attributed to the group collectively.
rows.anchor: قال الحريري المعنى لتتربص كل واحده منهن ثلاثة اقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هدى can mean tawhid, as in the objection “if we follow the monotheism with you.”
rows.anchor: وبمعنى التوحيد ﴿ إن نتبع الهدى معك ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هدى can mean the Sunna or inherited religious practice.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى السنة ﴿ وإنا على آثارهم مهتدون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هدى can mean to set aright or effect reform.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى الإصلاح ﴿ وأن الله لا يهدي كيد الخائنين ﴾

words: أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here هدًى means inspiration or guidance to each creature’s livelihood.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى الإلهام ﴿ أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى ﴾ هدى كلا فى معيشته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هدنا means “we repented.”
rows.anchor: وبمعنى التوبة ﴿ إنا هدنا إليك ﴾ أى تبنا

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says أسف usually means grief, but فلما آسفونا means “when they angered Us.”
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فارس فى كتاب الأفراد كل ما فى كتاب الله من ذكر الأسف فمعناه الحزن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains غضبان أسفا as “enraged.”
rows.anchor: وأما قوله فى قصة موسى عليه السلام ﴿ غضبان أسفا ﴾ فقال ابن عباس مغتاظا

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says بروج usually means stars, except in 4:78, where it means tall, fortified towers.
rows.anchor: وكل ما فى القرآن من ذكر البروج فإنها الكواكب

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says البر and البحر generally mean dry land and water; in 30:41 they mean countryside and inhabited areas.
rows.anchor: وما فى القرآن من ذكر البر والبحر فإنه يراد بالبحر الماء وبالبر التراب اليابس

rows.speaker: بعض علمائنا
rows.claim: Some scholars interpret corruption on land as Cain killing Abel, and corruption at sea as the king seizing every ship by force.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض علمائنا فى البر قتل ابن آدم أخاه

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says بخس means deficiency generally, but in “a paltry price” the commentators take it to mean unlawful.
rows.anchor: والبخس فى القرآن النقص مثل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says بعل means husband except in al-Saffat, where it means an idol.
rows.anchor: وما فى القرآن من ذكر البعل فهو الزوج

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says بكم usually means being unable to speak in faith despite a sound tongue; in two exceptions it means literal speechlessness.
rows.anchor: وما فى القرآن من ذكر البكم فهو الخرس عن الكلام بالإيمان

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says جثيا means gathered together throughout the Quran, except in 45:28, where each nation kneels on its knees.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن ﴿ جثيا ﴾ فمعنا جميعا إلا التى فى سورة الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in مستكبرين به may refer either to the Quran or to the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ مستكبرين به سامرا تهجرون ﴾ 6 يعني القرآن أو المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage cites Joseph’s “she seduced me” as an example of a pronoun whose antecedent is clear from the story.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ قال هي راودتني عن نفسي ﴾ 7

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Father, hire him” is another example where the pronoun’s referent is supplied by the narrative.
rows.anchor: يا أبت استأجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the deceased, though no deceased person was previously named; the inheritance opening makes one understood.
rows.anchor: الضمير يعود على الميت وان لم يتقدم له ذكر إلا انه لما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inheritance passage, منه refers to the inherited estate.
rows.anchor: اي من الموروث وهذا وجه آخر غير ما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in اتخذها returns to شيئا because the mocker treats some verses as though mocking all of them.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل اتخذه ردا للضمير إلى شيئا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another analysis takes شيئا to mean an ayah, which explains the feminine pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقيل شيئا بمعنى الاية لأن بعض الايات آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pronoun may refer to an unmentioned companion understood from the scene: here it refers to the hands accompanying necks in chains.
rows.anchor: وقد يعود الضمير على الصاحب المسكوت عنه لاستحضاره بالمذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in من عمره refers to the other person, tacitly evoked by contrast with the long-lived person.
rows.anchor: اي من عمر غير المعمر فاعيد الضمير على غير المعمر لان ذكر المعمر يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pronoun may return to only part of an earlier category: نساء refers to a subset of the children mentioned in the inheritance opening.
rows.anchor: وقد يعود الضمير على بعض ما تقدم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to divorced women, but the ruling concerns revocable divorce; jurists dispute whether this narrows the earlier general rule.
rows.anchor: فانه عائد على المطلقات مع إن هذا خاص بالرجعى وهل يقتضي ذلك تخصيص الاول فيه خلاف اصولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to silver, one part of the earlier mention, which represents all hoarded wealth.
rows.anchor: فان الفضة بعض المذكور فأغنى ذكرها عن ذكر الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same عمره example can instead be explained as a pronoun returning to the original wording rather than its intended meaning.
rows.anchor: وقد يعود على اللفظ الاول دون معناه كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning the pronoun to the meaning rather than the first wording in this example avoids requiring restriction of the earlier general category.
rows.anchor: ويستراح من الزام تخصيص الاول

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the dual pronoun follows the intended sense because this case is not framed as one, two, or plural; similarly, من may take agreement by meaning.
rows.anchor: قال الاخفش انما يثنى لان الكلام لم يقع على الواحد والاثنين والجمع فثنى الضمير الراجع إليها حملا على المعنى

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi explains the dual as permissible because من conveys number without distinguishing small from large.
rows.anchor: وقال الفارسي انما جازت من حيث كان يفيد العدد مجردا من الصغير والكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An impersonal pronoun whose antecedent is neither stated nor contextually known requires explanation by a word or clause; these include the pronoun of affair.
rows.anchor: السادس إلا يعود على مذكور ولامعلوم بالسياق أو غيره وهو الضمير المجهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular pronoun in نعم and بئس is explained by a word, while a clause explains the pronoun of affair or story.
rows.anchor: فالمفرد في نعم وبئس والجملة ضمير الشأن والقصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun of affair may be feminine when the clause that explains it has a feminine referent.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون مؤنثا اذا كان عائده مؤنثا كقوله تعالى

words: إنه من يأت ربه مجرما فإن له جهنم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening pronoun remains masculine although the clause mentions feminine Jahannam, because the intended sense is that a guilty arrival is punished with Hell.
rows.anchor: فذكر الضمير مع اشتمال الجملة على جهنم وهي مؤنثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A separation pronoun may be first, second, or third person and has syntactic case; a pronoun of affair is third person only and nominative.
rows.anchor: والفرق بينه وبين ضمير الفصل إن الفصل يكون على لفظ الغائب والمتكلم والمخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pronoun may refer to the generic kind of a thing: به refers to provisions in both gardens, encompassed by “what we were given before.”
rows.anchor: البحث الثالث قد يعود على لفظ شيء والمراد به الجنس من ذلك الشئ
